title: The planned Capitol-style session and Max Steiner's 'Over the Rainbow'
summary: The planned session of his new pieces yielded only 'Dalvatore' and half of 'Over the Rainbow'; Johnny Richards may have finished it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: During those periods-- that period--you were writing the more elaborate pieces of music?
San Francisco and Hollywood, all that stuff was written. It started in San Francisco and continued in Hollywood until the point that I left the band.
Tell me about the planned recording session and the one that finally came into being.

The planned recording session was the one of all the new music. It would have been "Dalvatore," "There's No You", "Out of This World," "Gray Suede," "Hey Look I'm Dancing," "Key F" and two more; "Memphis In June" and "Over The Rainbow." When I got back the only ones they had done were "Dalvatore" and half of "Over The Rainbow"; the other half was completed by--I find it hard to believe that it was Max Steiner. Why Max Steiner would have wanted to involve himself with the second half of a jazz band chart I could never begin to understand why.
Nobody else--I guess Jack McKenney--said that he thought it was Johnny
Richards, but Johnny Richards wasn't on the scene then, was he?
Yes he was. Johnny took my place.
As writer, and John was right there all the time.
